groups.title: Racket sports
groups.explanation: Each of these is played by hitting a ball or shuttle with a racket.

groups.title: Vegetables
groups.explanation: All four are vegetables grown in gardens and allotments.

groups.title: Sports played with a stick
groups.explanation: Each is a team game in which a stick moves the ball.

sources.excerpt: Racketlon, a racket sport quadrathlon, is a multisport competition in which participants compete in a series of four separate racket sports: table tennis, badminton, squash, and tennis.
Since 1992, the Padel World Championship has been held every two years, and each final has featured Argentina alongside either Spain or Brazil.
In 2005, a poll of 2,000 people revealed the courgette to be Britain's 10th most popular culinary vegetable.
It is closely related, but not identical, to the marrow; its fruit may be called marrow when mature.
Vegetable orchestras, such as the London Vegetable Orchestra use zucchini trumpets, butternut squash trombones, pumpkin drums and aubergine castanets.
Three closely related vegetables—elephant garlic, kurrat and Persian leek or tareh—are also cultivars of A.
Hockey is a family of stick sports where two opposing teams use hockey sticks to propel a ball or disk into a goal.
Lacrosse is a contact team sport played with a lacrosse stick and a lacrosse ball.

The final of the All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship was listed in second place by CNN in its "10 sporting events you have to see live", after the Olympic Games and ahead of both the FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship.
In shinty a player is allowed to play the ball in the air and use both sides of the stick.

editorNotes: Squash is the tile that fits twice, a racket game and the vegetable family that includes the marrow; the vegetable group is complete with marrow, courgette, aubergine and leek, so squash is counted as a sport. Marrow and leek have no second life here, and hurling and shinty are games alone.
